name: Minimum aperiodic peak sidelobe level, binary sequences

configuration_expansion_review.source: Nunn and Coxson (2008), Table 2, rows N=101 and N=102; source text excerpts and witness hashes saved under data/source/.
configuration_expansion_review.note: C01 retains its prior Sol acceptance. C02 and C03 require independent Sol acceptance.

source_review.definition: Binary aperiodic PSL. C01 length100 retained, new C02 length101 and C03 length102. Minimize the maximum absolute off-zero correlation, with all signs exactly +/-1.
source_review.primary_source: Sol downloaded https://www.norbertwiener.umd.edu/crowds/documents/best_known_binary.pdf and read Table2 (Codes with PSL=5). Its 101 and102 rows are exactly 1A5048216CCF18F83E910DD4C5 and2945A4F11CE44FF664850D182A. The trailing7 is the previous comparison result, not the reported score of these witnesses.
source_review.open_status: Brest et al. preprints.org/manuscript/202605.0907 v2, posted2026-07-28, distinguishes exact minima through61 and at64 from best-known results for larger lengths, citing Nunn-Coxson for71-105. This source review found no optimality proof for101/102. No exhaustive absence-of-proof claim is made.
source_review.independent_method: Sol ran both human programs. The task checker multiplies and sums signs; the separate Sol audit bit-packs signs and counts XOR mismatches for every lag. The exact peaks are5 for both, and the entire correlation arrays agree. Illegal signs are rejected and all returned score-claim fields are ignored.
source_review.admission: All five programs, strict replay, cold seed export, malformed witnesses, complete claim invariance and error/nonfinite/timeout controls passed for all3 configurations. Isolated -I single-file cold-start tests also pass. Source record witness hashes reconciled with actual archived bytes.
